clue.text: Kind pro offers to screen compound I'd best not reveal

indicators.note: a screen stands around something and hides it, so the other pieces wrap around the compound

parts.note: a mode is a kind or manner
pro means in favour of
bids are offers, as at an auction
a sty is the enclosed compound where pigs are kept

explanation.surface: A kindly professional hides some chemical compound and keeps quiet about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' reads as chemistry but is a pig pen; offers is not the link word here but a piece of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is the polite excuse for withholding a boast or a detail about oneself.

clue.text: In stalag with perhaps twenty or thirty prisoner restraints

indicators.note: a stalag was a German prison camp, so the next word is given in German

parts.note: German for with
twenty and thirty are multiples of ten, tens

explanation.surface: A prisoner of war shackled for twenty or thirty years in a camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Mittens is old slang for handcuffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Underworld slang calls handcuffs mittens, as they encase the hands.

clue.text: Fellow Animal Guide has brief to come back soon!

indicators.note: has means holds, so the three words hold the shortened word

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
a beast is an animal
a ranger guides visitors around a park

indicators.note: brief means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A college fellow with an animal guide has a brief to return soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' cut short leaves its first letter, which goes in just after the fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a friendly parting request that someone visit again before long.

clue.text: Have room for five letters or ninety degrees?

wordplay.note: the alphabet run S, T, U, V, W is five letters, and on a compass south to west is a quarter turn

explanation.surface: Can a space fit five letters, or is it a matter of angles?
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as S TO W; both halves of the wordplay describe that span.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to pack away, so a space that can stow something has room for it.

clue.text: React to sharp bite of lemon chicken?

parts.note: to yell is to react loudly
ow is the cry at a sharp bite

explanation.surface: Wincing at the tang of a lemon chicken dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Lemon here is a colour and chicken an adjective for cowardly; both mean the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is the colour of lemons and slang for cowardly, just like chicken.

clue.text: Ill due to repeatedly absorbing pressure, chose Exit

indicators.note: absorbing means the scrambled letters take in the pressure letter
ill means unwell or out of sorts, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word to is given twice

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: Sick from being pressured again and again, someone chose the way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill' looks like the definition of a sick person, but it is the anagram signal; the doubled word gives TOTO, and the P goes in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick Exit is to choose to leave a scheme or arrangement, withdrawing from it.

clue.text: Say "… this is to make an ass of me …" the upshot?

definitions.text: Say "… this is to make an ass of me …"
definitions.meaning: a line spoken by Bottom the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream after he is given an ass's head
the final result or crucial point

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the gist of a remark is that they are being made a fool of.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom is the Shakespeare character turned into an ass, so his speech is literally his line.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom line, the last figure in accounts, means the essential outcome.

clue.text: Fashion bar in our style for inside?

definitions.text: Fashion bar in our style for inside?

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped into a new order
bar means except, so the letters of in are left out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A designer wants a bar fitted in their own style inside the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IN out of the letters of 'our style for inside' and rearrange what is left. Read as a whole, the clue describes amateurs who fashion their own home interiors.
explanation.definitionFit: DIY enthusiasts make and fit things for their homes themselves rather than hiring tradespeople.

clue.text: The same answer, so minute's saved

parts.note: A is short for answer

indicators.note: something saved is kept safe inside

parts.note: such as in 'so great' and 'such greatness'
M is short for minute

explanation.surface: An exam tip: give the same answer and you save a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside SUCH, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: As much means an equal amount, as in 'I thought as much', the same.

clue.text: Food wrapper can frustrate

parts.note: a tin is a can
to foil a plan is to frustrate it

explanation.surface: A tin can wrap food yet also stop you getting at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin metal sheet is used in kitchens to cover and wrap dishes.

clue.text: It will reverse consumption with its choice selection

indicators.note: the word It itself is said to reverse, so read it back to front

parts.note: the word It, turned round
consumption is the old name for tuberculosis, TB
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something promises to undo the effects of eating with a careful choice of foods.
explanation.definitionFit: Titbits are small choice morsels, of food or of news, picked out for their appeal.

clue.text: Island having power and resources left

indicators.note: in an across entry, going left means reading from right to left

parts.note: someone able has the power and means to do something

explanation.surface: An island with electricity and supplies to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: Left looks like 'remaining' but sends ABLE backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is the Mediterranean isle where Napoleon was first exiled.

clue.text: Red meat is not generally well done

parts.words: Red meat is not generally well done
parts.note: surface: rare meat is rarely cooked through; setter's reading: the opening words want completing with the answer to make a health warning, and the answer is also an exclamation of praise

explanation.surface: A cook observes that red meat is usually served pink rather than cooked through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well done' is not cooking at all but congratulation; and the answer slots into the first five words to make a dietary truism.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a congratulation, used exactly like 'bravo' to someone who has achieved something.

clue.text: So sire can't have any bright individuals in school?

definitions.note: plural; the fish's plural is unchanged

wordplay.note: the dam, a horse's mother, keeps everything, so the sire gets none

explanation.surface: A father is barred from having any clever children at school.
explanation.walkthrough: A school is a shoal of fish, and the bright individuals are colourful fish, not pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Damselfish are small, vividly coloured reef fish that often swim in shoals.

clue.text: Main route down to Kent on holiday?

parts.note: Kent is in the South East of England
someone on holiday is away

explanation.surface: The road down to Kent when heading off on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is the sea in crosswords; Kent is the county in England's south-east corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaway is a shipping lane or channel, a route across or through the sea.

clue.text: Leave crust after boiling a lot of water

parts.note: fur is the scaly deposit hard water leaves in a kettle
a lough is an Irish lake

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave the crust behind when a lot of water has boiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Furlough is leave of absence, originally for soldiers, later also for laid-off workers.

clue.text: Bold, fine characteristic of Van Gogh

parts.note: F is short for fine, as on pencils
Van Gogh famously cut off part of his ear

explanation.surface: Boldness and fine work were hallmarks of Van Gogh's painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearless means without fear, a synonym of brave.

clue.text: French art retrospective: assess it among displays

indicators.note: looking back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
the run of words openly shows the letters sitting inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A review of a French exhibition invites you to weigh up the works on show.
explanation.walkthrough: A retrospective is also an art show, which is the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings by Henri Matisse, the French artist, can be called Matisses, as one might say 'two Picassos'.

clue.text: A taste of Madras when after spicy dish

indicators.note: a taste is a small sample, just the first bit

parts.note: first letter
as means when, as in 'as he left'
à la means after the style of

explanation.surface: A sample of a Madras curry and then another spicy dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Masala is a spice blend, and a dish cooked in such a sauce.

clue.text: With evacuation, American guests truly distressed

indicators.note: evacuating empties out the insides, so only the edge letters remain

parts.note: first and last letters
first and last letters
first and last letters

explanation.surface: American visitors upset at being made to leave a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Angsty means full of angst, anxious and troubled.

clue.text: Nursery's last howler damaged pot culture

indicators.note: the last means only the final letter is kept

parts.note: final letter
an own goal, OG, is a footballer's howler
hurt means damaged

explanation.surface: A child at nursery screams and breaks a pot of seedlings.
explanation.walkthrough: An own goal is scoring into your own net in football.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoghurt is a bacterial culture of milk, often sold in pots.

clue.text: Individual identifiers given up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a name identifies
a number, abbreviated No, also identifies

explanation.surface: A person's identifying details were handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, identifiers, supplies two pieces: a name and a number.
explanation.definitionFit: One-man means done by a single individual, as in a one-man band.

clue.text: It could be worth noticing walk breaking into run

indicators.note: one thing breaking into another goes inside it

parts.note: a sprint is a run; its first letter comes before the insert
a mall is a shaded public walk, as in London's Mall

explanation.surface: A runner is told it might pay to notice someone walking onto the track.
explanation.walkthrough: MALL goes inside SPRINT.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine print of a contract hides the terms you would be wise to read.

clue.text: Plant stone marker to indicate decline

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an iris, like the yellow one of riverbanks
second meaning: a flat paving slab used for paths and floors
third meaning: a small marker, as on a golf green or a page
fourth meaning: to tire or weaken

explanation.surface: Someone sets a stone as a marker to show where ground begins to slope away.
explanation.walkthrough: Four separate meanings of one short word, joined by 'to indicate'; 'plant' looks like a verb but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers an iris, a paving slab, a signalling banner or tab, and the verb for losing energy.

clue.text: The country's history's omitted from exam

indicators.note: something omitted is left out of the whole

parts.note: pastoral means of the countryside
history is the past

explanation.surface: A national history paper has been dropped from the exam syllabus.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, as in a language test.

clue.text: You'll have this on when receiving a delivery

definitions.text: You'll have this on when receiving a delivery

parts.words: You'll have this on when receiving a delivery
parts.note: surface: something you wear when a parcel arrives; setter's reading: a batsman facing a ball in cricket, with the on side of the field beside him

explanation.surface: Something you put on when the postman brings a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a delivery is a ball bowled, and the on side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg side is the cricket term for the on side, the half of the field where the batter's legs face.

clue.text: Cameo even greater in recital

indicators.note: a recital is spoken out, so the word goes by its sound

parts.note: more so means even greater

explanation.surface: A short role played to even greater effect in a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A morceau is a short piece of music or writing, a little gem like a cameo.

clue.text: Couple who had pianos well oiled

definitions.meaning: two composers who were both great pianists
rhyming slang for drunk, rhyming with pissed

explanation.surface: Two pianists whose instruments were kept in good order.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang: the composers' names rhyme with pissed, British slang for drunk; well oiled is also drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The two Romantic composers were both piano virtuosos, and their names make a slang term for intoxicated.
